title: Microtask Starvation Guard & Fair Task Scheduler
problemStatement: If recursive microtasks continually schedule more microtasks, the event loop locks up and macrotasks/UI renders never run. Implement `fairScheduler(tasks, maxMicrotasksPerYield)` that executes tasks via microtasks, but yields to a macrotask (`setTimeout`) after `maxMicrotasksPerYield` tasks to prevent UI starvation.
interviewTrap: Infinite microtasks (`while(true) queueMicrotask(...)`) cause complete page freeze because the event loop will never leave the microtask checkpoint to service browser renders or user clicks.

testCases.name: Processes large batch correctly with yields
testCases.testFn: const tasks = Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) => () => i); const res = await fairScheduler(tasks, 3); return res.length;

testCases.name: Allows interleaved macrotask execution during yields
testCases.testFn: let timerFired = false; setTimeout(() => { timerFired = true; }, 0); const tasks = Array.from({ length: 8 }, () => () => 1); await fairScheduler(tasks, 2); return timerFired;

details.name: Processes large batch correctly with yields
Allows interleaved macrotask execution during yields

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Because the event loop drains the microtask queue until it is completely empty before running any macrotask or browser rendering, recursively queueing microtasks causes *Microtask Starvation* (freezing the UI and starving I/O). A Fair Task Scheduler interleaves large batches by voluntarily yielding to the macrotask queue or scheduler API.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Process items in slices (chunk size, e.g. 10 items).
If remaining items exist, check elapsed time or chunk limit.
Yield control to the macrotask queue using `await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0))` or `scheduler.yield()`.
This allows interleaved macrotasks (user input, timeouts, UI rendering) to execute before resuming the batch.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: The browser renders frames (requestAnimationFrame and Paint) between macrotask turns.Draining microtasks without yielding blocks the main thread completely. Yielding to a macrotask gives the browser event loop opportunity to process the UI and other tasks.

complexity.time: O(N) total processing time for N items.
complexity.space: O(N) memory for queued task items.

edgeCasesHandled: Interleaving allows macrotasks scheduled concurrently to execute.
Large tasks (e.g. 1,000 items) finish completely without freezing the thread.
Graceful completion on empty or single-item queues.

specifications: W3C Scheduling APIs: scheduler.yield() and Prioritized Task Scheduling
HTML Living Standard §8.1.6.2 Processing model (Macrotask vs Microtask starvation risks)
verifiedRules: Microtasks starve macrotasks if chained infinitely without yield.
Yielding via setTimeout(0) or scheduler.yield breaks synchronous task monopolization.
